questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: If the network had fact-checked the story, it wouldn't be facing a lawsuit now.
If the network fact-checked the story, it wouldn't be facing a lawsuit now.
If the network had fact-checked the story, it wouldn't have faced a lawsuit now.
If the network had fact-checked the story, it won't face a lawsuit now.
questions.explanation: Mixed conditional: If + past perfect (past condition), would + base verb (present result): 'If the network had fact-checked..., it wouldn't be facing a lawsuit now.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Misinformation will keep spreading unless platforms won't verify sources.
Misinformation will keep spreading unless platforms verify sources.
Misinformation will keep spreading unless that platforms verify sources.
Misinformation will keep spreading without platforms verify sources.
questions.explanation: 'Unless' means 'if...not' and is followed by an affirmative clause: 'unless platforms verify sources.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Several misleading ads has been removed this year.
Several misleading ads have removed this year.
Several misleading ads have been removed this year.
Several misleading ads have being removed this year.
questions.explanation: Present perfect passive: have/has been + past participle: 'have been removed this year.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: This false claim should corrected immediately.
This false claim should being corrected immediately.
This false claim should be correct immediately.
This false claim should be corrected immediately.
questions.explanation: Modal passive: modal + be + past participle: 'should be corrected immediately.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence. (Direct: "Please verify your sources before publishing.")
options: The editor told us to verify our sources before publishing.
The editor told us verify our sources before publishing.
The editor said us to verify our sources before publishing.
The editor told us that verify our sources before publishing.
questions.explanation: Reported commands: tell + object + to + base verb: 'told us to verify our sources.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence. (Direct: "You should limit your screen time.")
options: She suggested to limit my screen time.
She suggested limiting my screen time.
She suggested me limiting my screen time.
She suggested that I limiting my screen time.
questions.explanation: 'Suggest' is followed by a gerund or 'that + subject + base verb': 'suggested limiting my screen time.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The magazine which she writes for it covers investigative journalism.
The magazine for that she writes covers investigative journalism.
The magazine for which she writes covers investigative journalism.
The magazine she writes for which covers investigative journalism.
questions.explanation: In formal style, the preposition moves before 'which': 'the magazine for which she writes.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The article publishing last week revealed shocking industry secrets.
The article published last week reveal shocking industry secrets.
The article which published last week revealed shocking industry secrets.
The article published last week revealed shocking industry secrets.
questions.explanation: A passive meaning reduces 'which was published' to the past participle alone: 'The article published last week...'

questions.topic: Modal verbs of past deduction (must have)
questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The company must have exaggerated its advertising claims.
The company must exaggerated its advertising claims.
The company must have exaggerate its advertising claims.
The company must has exaggerated its advertising claims.
questions.explanation: Past deduction: must have + past participle: 'must have exaggerated its claims.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The network should acted sooner to retract the false report.
The network should have acted sooner to retract the false report.
The network should have act sooner to retract the false report.
The network should has acted sooner to retract the false report.
questions.explanation: Past regret/criticism: should have + past participle: 'should have acted sooner.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Advertising spending rose significantly over the past decade.
Advertising spending has risen significantly over the past decade.
Advertising spending have risen significantly over the past decade.
Advertising spending have rose significantly over the past decade.
questions.explanation: 'Over the past decade' links the past to the present, so present perfect is used: 'has risen significantly.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: By the time the correction was published, the story went viral.
By the time the correction had published, the story went viral.
By the time the correction was published, the story have already gone viral.
By the time the correction was published, the story had already gone viral.
questions.explanation: The earlier of two past actions takes the past perfect: 'the story had already gone viral.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Media regulators are meeting next week to discuss new guidelines.
Media regulators meet next week to discuss new guidelines.
Media regulators will meeting next week to discuss new guidelines.
Media regulators are meet next week to discuss new guidelines.
questions.explanation: Present continuous expresses a fixed future arrangement: 'are meeting next week.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: She said she will release the documentary next year.
She said she would release the documentary next year.
She said she would released the documentary next year.
She said she would have release the documentary next year.
questions.explanation: In reported speech, 'will' shifts back to 'would': 'she said she would release the documentary.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: I wish news outlets take accuracy more seriously.
I wish news outlets have taken accuracy more seriously.
I wish news outlets took accuracy more seriously.
I wish news outlets would take accuracy more seriously as a rule.
questions.explanation: 'Wish' + past simple expresses regret about a present situation: 'I wish news outlets took accuracy more seriously.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: I wish the editor warned readers earlier about the bias.
I wish the editor have warned readers earlier about the bias.
I wish the editor would have warned readers earlier about the bias.
I wish the editor had warned readers earlier about the bias.
questions.explanation: 'Wish' + past perfect expresses regret about the past: 'I wish the editor had warned readers earlier.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: We had our advertisement reviewed by the regulatory board.
We had reviewed our advertisement by the regulatory board.
We had our advertisement review by the regulatory board.
We have our advertisement reviewed by the regulatory board last year.
questions.explanation: Causative form: have + object + past participle shows someone else did the action: 'had our advertisement reviewed.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Never before the channel had reached such a large audience.
Never before had the channel reached such a large audience.
Never before did the channel reached such a large audience.
Never before has the channel had reached such a large audience.
questions.explanation: Negative adverbials at the start trigger inversion: 'Never before had the channel reached...'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The regulator is looking the misleading advert into.
The regulator is looking in to the misleading advert.
The regulator is looking into the misleading advert.
The regulator is looking into to the misleading advert.
questions.explanation: 'Look into' means 'investigate' and is inseparable: 'looking into the misleading advert.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: What the industry urgently need are clearer advertising standards.
That the industry urgently needs is clearer advertising standards.
What the industry urgently needs is clearer advertising standards it.
What the industry urgently needs is clearer advertising standards.
questions.explanation: 'What' clefts take a singular verb when the complement is singular: 'What the industry needs is clearer standards.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Some outlets fact-check thoroughly, whereas others publish rumors.
Some outlets fact-check thoroughly, whereas others publishes rumors.
Some outlets fact-check thoroughly whereas, others publish rumors.
Some outlets fact-check thoroughly despite others publish rumors.
questions.explanation: 'Whereas' contrasts two clauses and is followed directly by the subject: 'whereas others publish rumors.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: In spite the backlash, the ad campaign continued.
In spite of the backlash, the ad campaign continued.
Despite of the backlash, the ad campaign continued.
In spite of the backlash, the ad campaign continued though.
questions.explanation: 'In spite of' is followed by a noun phrase: 'In spite of the backlash, the ad campaign continued.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: A number of studies has linked social media use to lower attention spans.
The number of studies have linked social media use to lower attention spans.
A number of studies have linked social media use to lower attention spans.
A great number of studies has linked social media use to lower attention spans.
questions.explanation: 'A number of' + plural noun takes a plural verb: 'a number of studies have linked...'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: She spoke in behalf of the entire editorial team.
She spoke on behalf for the entire editorial team.
She spoke behalf of the entire editorial team.
She spoke on behalf of the entire editorial team.
questions.explanation: 'On behalf of' means 'representing someone': 'she spoke on behalf of the team.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The introduction of stricter advertising rules reduced misleading claims significantly.
The introduce of stricter advertising rules reduced misleading claims significantly.
The introducing of stricter advertising rules reduced misleading claims significantly.
The introduction of stricter advertising rules reduce misleading claims significantly.
questions.explanation: Formal writing often nominalizes verbs into nouns: 'introduce' becomes 'the introduction of...'

questions.question: Which is the most appropriate formal opening line for an email requesting information about advertising rates?
options: I'm writing to ask you about your advertising rates, ok?
I am writing to enquire about your advertising rates.
Just wanted to know about your advertising rates.
Hey, tell me about your advertising rates.
questions.explanation: 'I am writing to enquire about...' is a standard formal opening for information requests.

questions.question: Which is the most appropriate opening line for a formal complaint about a misleading advertisement?
options: I'm writing because I'm really mad about your misleading ad.
I want to complain about your misleading ad, it's bad.
I am writing to express my concern about a misleading advertisement.
I am writing to express my concern about a misleading advertisement, ok.
questions.explanation: Formal complaints use measured language such as 'I am writing to express my concern about...'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The reaction to the campaign was extreme alarming.
The reaction to the campaign was extremely alarm.
The reaction to the campaign was very much alarming.
The reaction to the campaign was extremely alarming.
questions.explanation: 'Extremely' (adverb) modifies the adjective 'alarming': 'was extremely alarming.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The campaign reached a wide audience. Moreover, it boosted sales.
The campaign reached a wide audience, moreover it boosted sales.
The campaign reached a wide audience. Moreover it boosted sales.
The campaign reached a wide audience moreover, it boosted sales.
questions.explanation: 'Moreover' begins a new sentence and is followed by a comma: 'The campaign reached a wide audience. Moreover, it boosted sales.'

questions.question: Choose the correct question tag.
options: You'd support stricter ad regulations, didn't you?
You'd support stricter ad regulations, wouldn't you?
You'd support stricter ad regulations, would you?
You'd support stricter ad regulations, wouldn't it?
questions.explanation: A positive statement with 'would' takes a negative tag: 'You'd support..., wouldn't you?'
